If you drive a diesel, you're sitting on the biggest tuning opportunity available.

Why Diesels Gain More

Modern diesels are heavily detuned from the factory. The engine hardware can do much more — the software holds it back.

  • +25-40% more torque
  • +20-35% more power
  • 5-15% better fuel economy (when driving normally)

Popular Diesel Cars to Remap

  • BMW 320d: 190hp → ~230hp
  • BMW 330d: 265hp → ~330hp
  • Audi A6 3.0 TDI: 286hp → ~350hp
  • VW Golf 2.0 TDI: Excellent Stage 1 gains
  • Range Rover TDV6: 250hp → ~310hp
  • Ford Transit: More pulling power for loaded vans

title.raw: TCU Gearbox Tuning — Faster Shifts & Smoother Driving
title.rendered: TCU Gearbox Tuning — Faster Shifts & Smoother Driving

content.raw:
ECU remapping isn't just about the engine. Your gearbox has its own computer — the TCU (Transmission Control Unit) — and tuning it can transform how your car drives.

What Is TCU Tuning?

TCU tuning modifies the gearbox software to change how it behaves. We can adjust shift speed, shift points, torque limits, and launch control settings. It works alongside your ECU remap for a complete performance upgrade.

What Does TCU Tuning Do?

  • Faster shifts: Gear changes happen quicker, reducing shift time by up to 50%
  • Higher torque limits: The gearbox allows more power to pass through without going into protection mode
  • Optimised shift points: Holds gears longer under acceleration, shifts earlier when cruising
  • Smoother operation: Reduces jerkiness and hesitation in everyday driving
  • Launch control: Some cars get improved launch control calibration

Which Gearboxes Can Be Tuned?

  • ZF 8-speed (BMW, Jaguar, Land Rover): Excellent response to tuning
  • DSG/S-Tronic (VW, Audi, Skoda): Smoother shifts, better launch control
  • 9G-Tronic (Mercedes): Faster shifts, torque limit increase
  • Torque converter autos: Most modern autos can be tuned

Do I Need TCU Tuning with My ECU Remap?

If you've had an ECU remap and your gearbox is automatic, TCU tuning is highly recommended. The extra power from the remap can confuse the stock gearbox calibration, leading to delayed shifts or torque intervention. TCU tuning ensures the gearbox works with the new power, not against it.

Is TCU Tuning Safe?

Yes. We stay within the hardware's design limits. We're not asking the gearbox to do more than it can — we're just removing the software restrictions that hold it back.

How Much Does It Cost?

TCU tuning starts from £180 at MapKings, and can be done alongside your ECU remap in the same session.

content.raw:
You've heard remapping makes a difference, but what does it actually feel like? Here's what to expect before and after your ECU remap.

Before the Remap

Your car as it left the factory. It works fine, but it's deliberately held back. Manufacturers detune engines for several reasons:

  • Meet emissions regulations in every market
  • Account for poor fuel quality in some regions
  • Ensure reliability across all climate conditions
  • Create product differentiation between model variants

The engine has more potential than you're getting.

After the Remap — What Changes

Throttle response: The first thing you'll notice. The car reacts faster when you press the accelerator. No more delay or "spongy" feeling.

Torque: Stronger pull through the mid-range. Overtaking becomes effortless. Hills that used to require a downshift feel easier.

Power: More power across the entire rev range. You'll feel it especially in the 2,000-4,000 RPM zone where most driving happens.

Gearbox behaviour (auto): Smoother, quicker shifts. The gearbox adapts to the new power delivery. Some customers say it feels like a different car.

Fuel economy: Mixed results. If you drive the same way, many customers see 5-10% better MPG. If you use the extra power (most people do), economy stays about the same.

What Doesn't Change

  • Your car still looks the same — no visible modifications
  • It still runs on regular fuel (for Stage 1)
  • It still passes MOT
  • Normal servicing intervals stay the same

First Drive — What to Expect

Most customers notice the difference within the first few miles. The car feels more alive. The throttle is sharper, the pull is stronger, and the overall driving experience is more engaging. It's not a night-and-day transformation — it's more like your car finally drives the way it should have from the factory.

Real Results from MapKings Customers

  • BMW 330i: "The difference was noticeable immediately. Much more responsive, smoother to drive."
  • Audi A4 TDI: "Overtaking is so much easier now. The torque just pulls you forward."
  • VW Golf GTI: "It feels like the car I always wanted. Best money I've spent on it."

Experience It Yourself

Book your remap or use our vehicle gains calculator to see your car's potential. Call 07306 558428.

content.raw:
Mobile ECU remapping means we bring the workshop to you. No need to drive to a garage, leave your car all day, or arrange a lift home. Here's how it works.

How Mobile Remapping Works

  1. You book an appointment — choose a date, time, and location (home, workplace, anywhere)
  2. We arrive with our equipment — laptop, diagnostic tools, and ECU tuning hardware
  3. Diagnostic check — we scan your car for any existing faults before we start
  4. Read the ECU — we connect to your car's OBD port and read the current software
  5. Apply the tune — we upload the custom calibration to your ECU
  6. Test and verify — we run diagnostics again and do a test drive to confirm everything is perfect

How Long Does It Take?

  • Stage 1 remap: 1-2 hours
  • Stage 2 remap: 1.5-2.5 hours
  • DPF/EGR solutions: 1-3 hours depending on the service

What Do You Need From Me?

Just your car and the keys. We bring everything else. Ideally, the car should be parked somewhere with enough space for us to work safely. A driveway, car park, or quiet street is perfect.

Areas We Cover

  • Aylesbury, High Wycombe, Milton Keynes
  • Chesham, Amersham, Beaconsfield, Marlow
  • Princes Risborough, Wendover, Great Missenden
  • And everywhere in between — see full list

Is Mobile Remapping as Good as Workshop Tuning?

Yes. We use the same professional equipment that workshop-based tuners use. The tune quality is identical — the only difference is we come to you instead of you coming to us.

title.raw: ECU Remapping Myths Debunked — 10 Things People Get Wrong
title.rendered: ECU Remapping Myths Debunked — 10 Things People Get Wrong

content.raw:
There's a lot of misinformation about ECU remapping. Let's bust the most common myths.

Myth 1: Remapping Damages Your Engine

Reality: A professional remap stays within safe operating parameters. We don't push engines beyond their design limits — we optimise within them. The factory tune is deliberately conservative to meet emissions regulations across all markets. A proper tune unlocks what the engine can safely do.

Myth 2: You'll Fail Your MOT

Reality: A standard remap will pass MOT. The emissions stay within legal limits. What fails MOT is removing the DPF, catalytic converter, or AdBlue system — those are separate modifications.

Myth 3: Remapping Isn't Reversible

Reality: We always save your original ECU file. If you want to go back to stock, we can flash it back anytime. Takes about 30 minutes.

Myth 4: It Voids Your Warranty Completely

Reality: It voids the powertrain/engine warranty specifically. Other warranties (body, electrical, interior) are unaffected. Once your warranty expires, there's no downside.

Myth 5: All Remaps Are the Same

Reality: Huge difference between a custom tune and a generic file. A custom tune is read from YOUR car's ECU, adjusted for YOUR engine's condition, and verified with diagnostic data. A generic file could be from any car.

Myth 6: You Need New Exhaust/Intake for a Remap

Reality: For Stage 1, you need zero modifications. The stock hardware is fine. Exhaust and intake upgrades are for Stage 2 and above.

Myth 7: Remapping Kills Your Fuel Economy

Reality: The opposite is often true. A well-tuned engine operates more efficiently. Many customers report better MPG on motorway runs after a remap, especially diesel engines.

Myth 8: Diesel Cars Can't Be Remapped

Reality: Diesels are actually the BEST candidates for remapping. They have the most to gain because factory tunes are heavily detuned for emissions compliance.

Myth 9: You'll Notice the Difference Immediately

Reality: Actually, this one is TRUE. Most customers feel the difference within the first few miles. More responsive throttle, stronger pull through the rev range, and smoother power delivery.

Myth 10: Remapping Is Only for Boy Racers

Reality: Our most common customers are everyday drivers who want their car to feel better. More torque for overtaking, smoother acceleration, better fuel economy. It's about making your daily drive more enjoyable.

Get the Facts

content.raw:
Not all cars respond equally to remapping. Some engines have massive hidden potential, while others are already near their limits from the factory. Here are the best cars to remap in 2026.

BMW — The Remap King

BMW engines are legendary for their tuning potential. The B48 (2.0T) and B58 (3.0T) respond incredibly well to Stage 1 remaps.

  • BMW 330i (B48): Stock 252hp → ~310hp with Stage 1
  • BMW M340i (B58): Stock 374hp → ~430hp with Stage 1
  • BMW 320d (B47): Stock 190hp → ~230hp with Stage 1

Audi & VW Group — Huge Variety

The EA888 engine (found in Golf GTI, Audi A3, Octavia vRS) is one of the most tunable engines ever made.

  • VW Golf GTI (EA888): Stock 245hp → ~310hp Stage 1
  • Audi S3 (EA888): Stock 310hp → ~370hp Stage 1
  • Skoda Octavia vRS: Stock 245hp → ~310hp Stage 1
  • VW Golf R: Stock 320hp → ~380hp Stage 1

Mercedes — AMG Line Sweet Spots

  • A35 AMG: Stock 306hp → ~370hp Stage 1
  • C300 (M264): Stock 258hp → ~310hp Stage 1

Ford — Budget Performance

  • Fiesta ST (1.5T EcoBoost): Stock 200hp → ~240hp Stage 1
  • Focus ST (2.3T EcoBoost): Stock 280hp → ~330hp Stage 1

Diesel Remaps — Best Value

Diesel engines often see the biggest percentage gains because they're heavily detuned from the factory for emissions compliance.

  • BMW 330d: Stock 265hp → ~330hp, massive torque gains
  • Audi A6 3.0 TDI: Stock 286hp → ~350hp
  • Range Rover Sport TDV6: Stock 250hp → ~310hp

Cars That Don't Remap Well

  • Naturally aspirated petrol engines (minimal gains)
  • Very old diesels without modern ECU management
  • Cars already running aggressive factory maps (some AMG/M models)

Car remapping prices in the UK range from £50 to £500+. But price alone doesn't tell you much. Here's what you're actually paying for and what to watch out for.

Average UK Remap Prices (2026)

Stage Typical Price What You Get
Stage 1 £200-£350 Software-only tune, +20-40% power
Stage 2 £250-£450 Tune for modified cars, +40-60% power
Stage 3 £500+ Built engine calibration, +60-100% power

Why Prices Vary So Much

The cheapest remaps (£50-£100) are usually generic files downloaded from the internet. They're not tailored to your car and can cause problems. A proper remap involves:

  • Reading your specific ECU software version
  • Custom calibration based on your car's condition
  • Diagnostic checks before and after
  • Test drive to verify results
  • Backup of your original file

Our Equipment

We use industry-leading tools for all our remapping work:

  • Alientech — Professional ECU tuning and programming tools
  • Magic Motorsport Flex — Advanced ECU, TCU, and gearbox tuning solution

Every remap file we create is custom-made for your specific vehicle — never generic, never off-the-shelf. We read your ECU's original data, calibrate it for your car's condition and your performance goals, then test and verify the results.

What MapKings Charges

  • Stage 1: £180 — custom tune, standard engine
  • Stage 2: £200 — tune for modified cars with bolt-ons
  • Stage 3: Price on application
  • DPF/EGR/AdBlue solutions: From £150

We're cheaper than most competitors because we're mobile — no workshop overhead. Same quality tune, lower price.

title.rendered: Is ECU Remapping Legal in the UK? — 2026 Guide

content.raw:
One of the first questions people ask about ECU remapping is whether it's legal. The short answer: yes, ECU remapping is completely legal in the UK. But there are some things you need to know.

Is Remapping Legal?

ECU remapping is legal for road vehicles in the UK. There is no law that prohibits modifying your engine's ECU calibration. Thousands of cars on UK roads are remapped.

Do I Need to Tell My Insurance?

Yes. Any modification that changes your vehicle's performance must be declared to your insurance company. Failure to do so could void your policy. Most insurers will cover a remap — it typically adds a small amount to your premium (often £50-£100/year).

Will It Pass an MOT?

A properly done remap will not affect your MOT. Your emissions will still pass because the tune is calibrated to stay within legal limits. However, if you've done a DPF delete or cat removal alongside the remap, that will fail the MOT.

What About the Warranty?

A remap will void your manufacturer's engine/powertrain warranty. If your car is still under warranty, consider this carefully. Once the warranty expires, there's nothing stopping you.

What Makes a Remap Illegal?

Remapping itself is legal. What's NOT legal:

  • Removing or bypassing the DPF (fines up to £1,000 for cars, £2,500 for vans)
  • Removing the catalytic converter
  • Disabling AdBlue systems on vehicles that require them
  • Tampering with emissions equipment

Professional vs Cheap Remaps

A professional remap from a reputable tuner like MapKings is done with proper diagnostic checks, stays within safe parameters, and is fully reversible. Cheap "pop and bang" remaps or eBay files can cause MOT failures and engine damage.

Book a Legal, Professional Remap

Book your remap with MapKings — fully legal, fully reversible, and done right. Call 07306 558428.

title.rendered: DPF Cleaning Near Me — Signs Your DPF Is Blocked & What to Do

content.raw:
If your DPF warning light is on, your car has lost power, or you're seeing poor fuel economy, your diesel particulate filter might be blocked. Here's what to do about it.

What Is a DPF?

Your Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) sits in the exhaust system and captures soot particles from diesel combustion. It's designed to self-clean through a process called regeneration — burning off the soot at high temperatures during longer drives.

Signs Your DPF Is Blocked

  • DPF warning light on the dashboard
  • Loss of power or limp mode
  • Poor fuel economy
  • Strong diesel smell
  • Failed MOT on emissions
  • Engine management light on

Why DPFs Get Blocked

Short trips and city driving are the biggest cause. If you only do short journeys, the exhaust never gets hot enough for regeneration to complete. The soot builds up until the filter is clogged.

DPF Cleaning Options

Forced regeneration: We force the engine to run a regeneration cycle. Works for partially blocked DPFs.

Off-car cleaning: We remove the DPF and professionally clean it. The most thorough method for heavily blocked filters.

DPF delete (off-road only): We can remove the DPF software for off-road/track vehicles. Not legal for road use in the UK.

How Much Does DPF Cleaning Cost?

DPF cleaning typically costs £150-£350 depending on the severity. At MapKings, we offer mobile DPF cleaning across Buckinghamshire — we come to your location.

Prevention Tips

  • Take your car on a 30+ minute motorway drive at least once a week
  • Don't ignore the DPF warning light
  • Use the correct engine oil (low-ash spec)
  • Keep up with servicing

Book DPF Cleaning

DPF problems? Book a mobile DPF clean or call 07306 558428. We cover all of Buckinghamshire.

title.rendered: Stage 1 vs Stage 2 Remap — Which Is Right for You?

content.raw:
Choosing between a Stage 1 and Stage 2 remap is one of the most common questions we get. Here's everything you need to know to make the right decision for your car and budget.

What Is a Stage 1 Remap?

A Stage 1 remap is a software-only tune on a completely standard engine. No hardware modifications needed. We read your ECU, adjust the calibration, and write it back with optimised settings.

  • Cost: £180 at MapKings
  • Power gains: Typically +20-40% more power and torque
  • Hardware required: None
  • Reversible: Yes — we can revert to stock at any time
  • Suitable for: Daily drivers who want more performance without any modifications

What Is a Stage 2 Remap?

A Stage 2 remap is calibrated for cars with supporting hardware modifications. Common Stage 2 mods include a performance downpipe, upgraded intercooler, cold air intake, or decat pipe.

  • Cost: £200 at MapKings
  • Power gains: Typically +40-60% more power and torque
  • Hardware required: Downpipe, intercooler, intake, or similar
  • Reversible: Yes, but hardware mods would need to be removed separately
  • Suitable for: Enthusiasts who've already invested in bolt-on modifications

Which Should You Choose?

Go Stage 1 if: Your car is completely standard, you want a noticeable improvement without spending money on parts, or you're leasing the car and want a reversible upgrade.

Go Stage 2 if: You've already fitted a downpipe, intercooler, or intake. A Stage 2 tune will maximise the benefit of those mods. Without the hardware, a Stage 2 map on a standard car can actually cause problems.

Can You Go Straight to Stage 2?

Not without the hardware. A Stage 2 calibration expects increased airflow and cooling. Running it on a standard engine can cause excessive exhaust gas temperatures, boost spikes, or limp mode. Always fit the hardware first, then get the tune.

What About Stage 3?

Stage 3 is for fully built engines — hybrid turbos, upgraded fuelling, forged internals. This is a serious performance build and pricing is on application. Most road cars will never need Stage 3.

Book Your Remap

Not sure which stage is right for you? Book a free consultation and we'll assess your car and recommend the best option. Call 07306 558428.

If you're considering an ECU remap for your car in Buckinghamshire, one of the first questions you'll have is: how much does it cost? This guide breaks down typical pricing, what affects the cost, and what you get for your money.

How Much Does ECU Remapping Cost?

In Buckinghamshire, ECU remapping typically costs between £180 and £350 for a Stage 1 remap. At MapKings Performance, our pricing is straightforward:

  • Stage 1 (software only): £180 — No hardware changes needed. Adds 20-40% more power and torque on a standard engine.
  • Stage 2 (bolt-on mods): £200 — For cars with a downpipe, intercooler, or intake. Bigger gains, 40-60% more power.
  • Stage 3 (built engine): Price on application — Full performance spec with hybrid turbos and upgraded internals.

What Affects the Price?

Several factors influence what you'll pay for an ECU remap:

  • Your vehicle make and model — Some ECUs are easier to read and write than others. Popular cars like BMW, Audi, and VW are typically straightforward.
  • The type of remap — A basic Stage 1 is cheaper than a Stage 2 or Stage 3 which requires supporting hardware.
  • Whether it's mobile or workshop-based — Mobile services like ours save you the trip. We come to your home or workplace anywhere in Buckinghamshire.
  • The tuner's experience — Cheap remaps from unknown tuners can cause engine damage. Always choose a reputable specialist.

Is a Cheap Remap Worth It?

You'll see ECU remaps advertised online for as little as £50-£100. These are usually generic file downloads — not custom-tuned to your specific engine. A proper remap involves reading your ECU, adjusting the calibration, and writing it back with settings tailored to your car. Generic files can cause:

  • Excessive exhaust gas temperatures
  • Increased fuel consumption
  • Transmission damage on automatics
  • MOT failures

At £180 for a Stage 1, MapKings offers professional-grade remapping at a fair price. Every tune is done on-site with proper diagnostic checks before and after.

What's Included in the Price?

Every MapKings remap includes:

  • Full diagnostic scan before tuning
  • Custom calibration for your specific vehicle
  • Test drive to verify the results
  • Before/after power estimates
  • Free revert to stock if you're not happy

Areas We Cover

We offer mobile ECU remapping across all of Buckinghamshire including Aylesbury, High Wycombe, Milton Keynes, Chesham, Amersham, Beaconsfield, Marlow, Princes Risborough, and surrounding areas. We also cover parts of Oxfordshire, Hertfordshire, and Berkshire.

Book Your Remap
